jobDescription: The marketing data warehouse feeds the company's campaign reporting and attribution models. The Analytics Engineer builds and maintains the warehouse's transformation models, reviews the marketing analysts' model contributions, runs the data quality checks and resolves their failures, supports the marketing analysts with modelling questions, and documents each model's limitations. Model release approval stays with the analytics engineering lead. The role requires mentoring analysts who are new to the modelling framework. Reports to the analytics engineering lead; works with the marketing analysts, the data platform team and the attribution modelling team.
requirements: Builds and maintains transformation models in the warehouse under the modelling framework's standard.
Reviews the marketing analysts' model contributions and mentors analysts new to the framework.
Runs the data quality checks and resolves their failures under the data quality procedure.
Coordinates model releases, with approval staying with the analytics engineering lead, and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents each model's limitations and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Analytics engineer on the marketing data warehouse of a consumer software company for three years, building and maintaining the warehouse's transformation models under the modelling framework's standard; about ninety models in the period, each on a merge request in my name.

Reviewed the marketing analysts' model contributions as one of the team's two reviewers and mentored the analysts new to the framework through the onboarding sessions; the review records and the onboarding attendance for eleven analysts are in the repository, with the analysts' first merged contributions logged against their onboarding.
Ran the data quality checks each day and resolved their failures under the data quality procedure, with the failure log recording each resolution.
Coordinated model releases through the release checklist; the release approval was the analytics engineering lead's, recorded on the checklist together with which checks were mine.
Wrote the limitation note and the hand-over conditions of each model in its documentation page.

Work sample: two merge requests with review records, the onboarding attendance log with the analysts' first contributions, one week's data quality failure log and one release checklist with its approval, with the repository references as a verification trail.
Interviewer 2 note: he seemed arrogant and a bit abrasive when the junior interviewer asked a basic question; my impression is he's not a team player and would be difficult to work with as a mentor.
Analytics engineering lead pre-read: two analysts left last year citing a hostile reviewer, so the packet should tell us whether he can mentor without putting people off.

propositions.text: The candidate built and maintained about ninety transformation models on a consumer software company's marketing data warehouse for three years under the modelling framework's standard, each on a merge request in his name, and ran the daily data quality checks with the failures resolved under the data quality procedure.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the merge requests and the failure log document the models and the quality checks.

propositions.text: The candidate reviewed the marketing analysts' model contributions as one of the team's two reviewers and mentored eleven analysts new to the framework through the onboarding sessions, with their first merged contributions logged against their onboarding.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the review records and the onboarding log document the reviews and the mentoring.

propositions.text: The interviewer's impression shows that the candidate is not a team player and would be difficult to work with as a mentor.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records an impression of manner in one exchange, not an observed job event; the review records and the onboarding log are the documented evidence and they show eleven analysts mentored to their first merged contribution.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions are documented in the model documentation pages but not for the review duties passed to the second reviewer during absences.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interviewer's impression as a signal to verify with a concrete example; do not present an impression of manner in one exchange as evidence about mentoring, which the review records and the onboarding log document directly.
followUpTargets: Ask for one review thread with a new analyst and the analyst's first merged contribution, and ask the interviewer which specific exchange prompted the impression.
